qualityChecks.reason: The top-level extra spread replaces the default server object. Explicit watch:null in the actual full HTTP server options restores the intended watcher setting for both compatibility and public-durable compositions without changing middleware mode or other merge behavior. Installed Vite 8.1.5 selects NoopWatcher for exactly null.

New assertions run inside the existing try/finally. Failure still awaits server.close. NoopWatcher supports the existing asynchronous close path. Existing idempotent close, cache cleanup, database disposal and global fetch restoration remain byte-identical; the audited public recovery test checks close identity, restored fetch and removed cache.

Loopback host, strict port, CORS, allowed hosts, filesystem allow/deny policy, outbound blocker, origin/nonce/auth/private-asset checks and provider/budget assertions are unchanged. Exact inverse edits recover baseline bytes. The original 45000 ms recovery clock still includes harness startup. No production source, timeout, skip or assertion weakening is present.

Assertions inspect the effective configuration and actual watcher on a real started harness. The null assertion prevents a temporarily empty asynchronous FSWatcher from falsely satisfying getWatched alone. This directly catches the shallow-override regression without depending on timing or watcher class names. The retained RED fails on undefined versus null. Existing integration tests cover both compositions.
